TopNavigation5.summary: Site header: logo on the left, up to six centred text links and one outline action button; collapses to a menu button on mobile.
bestFor: the first element of any marketing page
sites with 3-5 top-level sections
avoidWhen: the host app already renders its own header
you need dropdown menus or more than six links
notes: Set logoSrc (an image your app serves, e.g. /logo.svg) or brandName (a text wordmark). With neither, it shows the Acme placeholder logo.
Mark the current page's link with active: true.
on.action is the outline button (sign in, log in, get started). Set actionLabel to "" to hide it.

Banner10.summary: Thin announcement bar on a muted background: info icon, bold highlight, one-sentence message, optional link and a close button.
bestFor: a launch, event or policy notice above the navigation
one short message with a link to details
avoidWhen: the message needs more than one sentence
there is nothing time-sensitive to announce
notes: Place it first, above TopNavigation5.
The close button hides the banner locally; bind on.dismiss only to remember the dismissal.
highlight is the bold lead-in (e.g. "New:"); a space is added after it.

Benefits13.summary: Centred heading over a grid of bordered cards, each with a round icon, a title and a short description; three columns on desktop, two on tablet, one on mobile.
bestFor: explaining 3, 6 or 9 product benefits right after the hero or navigation
features that each fit in one sentence
avoidWhen: you have only one or two points (use the heading description)
benefits need screenshots
notes: Use 3, 6 or 9 benefits so the three-column grid has no gaps.
icon is one of: prioritize, integrate, data, analytics, workflow, team, speed, security, privacy, time, launch, ai. Omitted icons cycle through that list.

Testimonials11.summary: Centred heading over a grid of quote cards, each with large quote marks, the quote, and the person's avatar, name and role; three columns on desktop.
bestFor: social proof from 3 or 6 customers
quotes of one to three sentences
avoidWhen: you have a single quote (use one card only if the page needs it)
quotes run longer than three sentences
notes: Use 3 or 6 testimonials so the grid has no gaps.
Put the company in role, e.g. "VP Engineering, Fieldwork".
Without imageSrc the avatar shows the person's initials.

Pricing8.summary: Centred heading over one to four plan cards: name, short description, large price with period, a checklist of features (optional tooltips) and a full-width button; the featured plan gets a primary border and solid button.
bestFor: two to four subscription plans
comparing plans by a short feature list
avoidWhen: you need a feature comparison table
pricing is fully custom (use CTA9 with a contact action)
notes: The grid fits the plan count: 1 plan is centred, 2 sit side by side, 3 or 4 fill the row.
price is display text: "$29", "Free" or "Custom". period defaults to "/month"; set "" to hide it.
Mark one plan featured: true.

on.select fires for every plan button. Bind selectedPlan to state ({"$bindState": "/pricing/selectedPlan"}) and pass {"$state": "/pricing/selectedPlan"} in the action params to know which plan was chosen.

FAQs4.summary: Centred tagline and heading over a single-open accordion of questions, followed by a one-line support prompt with a link.
bestFor: 4-8 common questions before the closing CTA or after pricing
answers of one to three sentences
avoidWhen: answers need lists, tables or images
you have fewer than three questions
notes: FAQs4 has no description prop.
Set supportText and supportLinkLabel to "" to remove the support line.

Team6.summary: Centred heading over a grid of member cards: a large square portrait beside the name and title, with a primary accent line.
bestFor: an about page or company section with 3-9 people
leadership or founding teams
avoidWhen: you have more than 12 people
you have no portraits (initials are a fallback, not a design)
notes: Use 3, 6 or 9 members so the grid has no gaps.
Without imageSrc the portrait shows the person's initials.

NewsletterSignup5.summary: Rounded muted panel: heading and description on the left, an email field with a subscribe button and a privacy note on the right; stacks on mobile.
bestFor: collecting email sign-ups near the end of a page or blog post
avoidWhen: it would sit next to another panel (CTA9 or another NewsletterSignup5)
you need more than an email address (use Contact11)
notes: Bind email to state ({"$bindState": "/newsletter/email"}) and pass {"$state": "/newsletter/email"} in the on.submit params; otherwise the action cannot see the address.
The field is required and must be an email address before on.submit fires.

Contact11.summary: Centred heading over a narrow form: name, email and message fields, a privacy consent checkbox with a link, and a full-width submit button.
bestFor: a contact or support page
sales enquiries after pricing
avoidWhen: you only need an email address (use NewsletterSignup5)
the form needs extra fields
notes: Bind values to state ({"$bindState": "/contact"}) and pass {"$state": "/contact"} in the on.submit params; the action receives {name, email, message, consent}.
Set consentText and privacyLabel to "" to remove the consent row.
Use one Contact11 per page: its fields have fixed ids.
The heading sits in a narrow column; keep it under 44 characters.

CTA9.summary: Full-width band on the primary colour: centred heading, optional description and one button with an arrow.
bestFor: the closing call to action, right before the footer
one clear next step (start trial, book demo)
avoidWhen: you need two buttons
it would sit next to another panel (NewsletterSignup5)
notes: Use one CTA9 per page, usually last before Footer4.

Footer4.summary: Site footer: separator, logo with a one-line description and social icons on the left, up to four link columns, then a copyright line.
bestFor: the last element of any marketing page
avoidWhen: the host app already renders its own footer
notes: Set logoSrc (an image your app serves, e.g. /logo.svg) or brandName (a text wordmark). With neither, it shows the Acme placeholder logo.
social items without href render as plain icons; set href, or "social": [] to remove the icons.
